    event_tx: [Sender](https://docs.rs/tokio/1.52.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tokio/sync/mpsc/bounded/struct.Sender.html)<[AgentEvent](https://docs.rs/enum.AgentEvent.html)>,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[RunResult](https://docs.rs/struct.RunResult.html), [AgentError](https://docs.rs/enum.AgentError.html)>

Run the agent with provider-facing prompt content derived from typed runtime appends, while persisting those appends according to their roles.

`injected_context` carries host-attached ambient context for the direct
(non-runtime) path: each entry materializes as a separate typed
injected-context user-channel message immediately before the turn’s
user message. When `typed_turn_appends` is non-empty the runtime
authored every transcript append for this turn (injected context
arrives as `InjectedContext`-role appends), so passing both is a
caller error — exactly one lowering owner per mode.

[Source](https://docs.rs/meerkat-core/0.7.12/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/meerkat_core/agent/runner.rs.html#1169)#### pub async fn [run_pending](https://docs.rs#method.run_pending)(&mut self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[RunResult](https://docs.rs/struct.RunResult.html), [AgentError](https://docs.rs/enum.AgentError.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/meerkat-core/0.7.12/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/meerkat_core/agent/runner.rs.html#1169)

#### pub async fn [run_pending](https://docs.rs#method.run_pending)(&mut self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[RunResult](https://docs.rs/struct.RunResult.html), [AgentError](https://docs.rs/enum.AgentError.html)>

Run the agent using the pending continuation boundary already in the session.

This is useful when the session has been pre-populated with a continuation
boundary (for example a deferred first-turn user message or staged callback
tool results). Unlike `run()`, this method does NOT add a new user message;
it runs directly from the session’s current state.

Returns `NoPendingBoundary` when generated pending-continuation
authority does not admit the current transcript tail.

`initial_tool_visibility_state`).

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.tool_access_policy)

`tool_access_policy: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[ToolAccessPolicy](https://docs.rs/enum.ToolAccessPolicy.html)>Per-launch call-level tool access policy (the existing
[ meerkat_core::ops::ToolAccessPolicy](https://docs.rs/enum.ToolAccessPolicy.html) vocabulary).

Resolved into the sealed [ meerkat_core::ToolExecutionPolicy](https://docs.rs/meerkat-core/0.7.12/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/meerkat_core/tool_execution_policy/struct.ToolExecutionPolicy.html) and
applied as the OUTERMOST dispatcher composition: execution of a denied
tool fails with an ordinary

`access_denied` tool error while the
LLM-visible tool list (`tools()`/`tool_catalog()`) stays byte-identical
(no prompt-cache prefix change). `Inherit` must be resolved by the
spawn chain before build; an unresolved `Inherit` fails the build
closed with a typed error. The effective policy is persisted into
`SessionMetadata.tooling.tool_access_policy` so children can inherit
it transitively.## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

### impl [AgentFactory](https://docs.rs/struct.AgentFactory.html)

Create a minimal factory for environments without filesystem access (e.g. wasm32).

All agent resources must be provided via `AgentBuildConfig` overrides
(`tool_dispatcher_override`, `session_store_override`, etc.).
Filesystem-dependent methods are not available.

Create a new factory with the required session store path.

The default file-backed TokenStore is attached when it opens cleanly.
OAuth-backed bindings read persisted tokens written by `rkat auth login`
and REST/RPC OAuth completion handlers out of the box. If the default
TokenStore fails to open (for example a corrupt credential backend),
the typed open fault is retained and the first provider resolution
fails with `FactoryError::TokenStore` — never silently degraded to
`InteractiveLoginRequired`.

Resolve the token store to attach to a `ResolverEnvironment`.

`Detached` → `Ok(None)`, `Attached` → `Ok(Some(store))`, and a
retained default-store open failure propagates as the typed
[ FactoryError::TokenStore](https://docs.rs/enum.FactoryError.html#variant.TokenStore) fault — provider resolution with a
faulted credential backend fails closed (mirroring the REST
surface, which fails startup on the same condition) instead of
proceeding with silently-absent persisted-auth truth.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/meerkat/factory.rs.html#3717-5752)

#### pub async fn [build_agent](https://docs.rs#method.build_agent)(
    &self,
    build_config: [AgentBuildConfig](https://docs.rs/struct.AgentBuildConfig.html),
    config: &[Config](https://docs.rs/struct.Config.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[DynAgent](https://docs.rs/type.DynAgent.html), [BuildAgentError](https://docs.rs/enum.BuildAgentError.html)>

Build a fully-configured, type-erased agent ready to run.

This method consolidates the agent construction pipeline that was previously repeated across all surfaces (CLI, REST, MCP server): load config, resolve provider/model, check API key, create LLM client + adapter, build tool dispatcher, create comms runtime, compose tools with comms, resolve hooks, build system prompt, wire AgentBuilder, and set SessionMetadata.

Public facade builds intentionally derive these defaults from
`Config.provider_tools` and the model profile. Use `provider_params` for
explicit per-build provider overrides. Calling this standalone-only
injection method makes `try_build` return a configuration error instead
of silently dropping the supplied defaults.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.max_tokens_per_turn)

`None` means “inherit / use the template default”; an explicit value is

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.provider_params)

`provider_params: `[ProviderParamsCarrier](https://docs.rs/meerkat-core/0.7.12/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/meerkat_core/lifecycle/run_primitive/struct.ProviderParamsCarrier.html)Typed provider parameter carrier (explicit overrides + build-derived provider-native tool defaults).

Parsed FAIL-CLOSED at config ingress: a malformed or unknown-keyed
provider-params shape is rejected when the config is read, never
deferred to the first LLM call. The explicit `params` half is
persisted; `tool_defaults` is `#[serde(skip)]` inside the carrier and
re-derived on every build (including resume) from
`Config.provider_tools` + `ModelProfile.supports_web_search`, so config
changes (e.g. disabling web search) take effect immediately on resumed
sessions. The per-turn effective params come from the carrier’s typed
field-wise merge ([ ProviderParamsCarrier::effective_params](https://docs.rs/meerkat-core/0.7.12/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/meerkat_core/lifecycle/run_primitive/struct.ProviderParamsCarrier.html#method.effective_params)).

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.output_schema)

`output_schema: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[OutputSchema](https://docs.rs/struct.OutputSchema.html)>Output schema for structured output extraction.

When set, the agent will perform an extraction turn after completing the agentic work, forcing the LLM to output validated JSON. The main response text remains the committed agentic output; extraction populates structured output on success or extraction error details on failure.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.structured_output_retries)

`structured_output_retries: `[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)Maximum retries for structured output validation failures.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.extraction_prompt)

`extraction_prompt: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>Custom prompt for the structured output extraction turn.

When `output_schema` is set, this prompt is sent as a user message
after the agentic loop to elicit schema-valid JSON. Defaults to a
built-in prompt if `None`.

# AuthBindingRef in meerkat - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/meerkat/0.7.12/meerkat/struct.AuthBindingRef.html

```
pub struct AuthBindingRef {
    pub realm:
```
[RealmId](https://docs.rs/meerkat-core/0.7.12/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/meerkat_core/connection/struct.RealmId.html),
    pub binding: [BindingId](https://docs.rs/meerkat-core/0.7.12/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/meerkat_core/connection/struct.BindingId.html),
    pub profile: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[ProfileId](https://docs.rs/meerkat-core/0.7.12/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/meerkat_core/connection/struct.ProfileId.html)>,
    pub origin: [BindingOrigin](https://docs.rs/meerkat-core/0.7.12/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/meerkat_core/connection/enum.BindingOrigin.html),
}## Expand description

Session-facing reference to a binding inside a realm.

`AuthBindingRef` is purely structural — it does NOT carry a `"realm:binding"`
string form. Wave-b deleted `parse` and `Display` so that no code path
accidentally ferries the opaque join through the runtime. CLI input that
arrives as `"realm:binding[:profile]"` must be split at the CLI boundary
and constructed field-by-field.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

`binding: `[BindingId](https://docs.rs/meerkat-core/0.7.12/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/meerkat_core/connection/struct.BindingId.html)[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.profile)

`profile: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[ProfileId](https://docs.rs/meerkat-core/0.7.12/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/meerkat_core/connection/struct.ProfileId.html)>[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.origin)

`origin: `[BindingOrigin](https://docs.rs/meerkat-core/0.7.12/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/meerkat_core/connection/enum.BindingOrigin.html)Whether this ref names a configured durable identity or the synthetic
env-var fallback. Defaults to [ BindingOrigin::Configured](https://docs.rs/meerkat-core/0.7.12/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/meerkat_core/connection/enum.BindingOrigin.html#variant.Configured) for back-read
of rows persisted before the discriminant existed.
